body.statement: Under the compact Laplace class and regime sampling, the certified construction is computable and satisfies \(\inf_{G\in\mathcal F}\inf_{P\in K_G}\Pr_P\{G\in\widehat{\mathcal C}_m\}\ge1-\alpha\) for every \(m\). Moreover, for every fixed \(\delta>0\), uniformly over \(P\in\bigcup_{G\in\mathcal F}K_G\), the probability that \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_m\) contains any \(G'\) with \(\inf_{Q\in K_{G'}}d(P,Q)\ge\delta\) tends to zero. The proof must derive the simultaneous real-and-imaginary Hoeffding radius \(\epsilon_m\), the feature tail \(2^{1-J_m}\), compactness, explicit inverse-resolvent moduli, and termination and consistency of certified global optimization.
body.justification: This rung propagates structural uncertainty through honest graph supersets without recovering or separating latent sources.
body.gap: Schkoda and Drton test necessary latent-SEM rank restrictions, and Wang et al. invert tests for acyclic orderings; neither provides full-law test inversion for intersecting compact latent cyclic intervention models.
body.consumer: A finite perturbation study can report a confidence superset of hidden feedback graphs and discard every candidate separated from the population response laws by a scientifically meaningful margin.
